packages/show-planner/package.json.content: The package points its entry points at `./dist` but declares neither a `files` whitelist nor an `exports` map. Without `files`, publishing will ship sources, tsconfig, and any local artifacts instead of just the built output; without `exports`, the subpath/entrypoint surface is implicit and consumers on strict ESM resolution can disagree with `main`/`types`. Add a `files: ["dist"]` whitelist and an explicit `exports` map (with matching `types`/`import` conditions).

There is no `prepare`/`prepublishOnly` hook, so nothing guarantees `dist/index.js` / `dist/index.d.ts` exist before the package is consumed or published. If a consumer installs or links this package before `yarn build` has run (or dist is absent from the tarball), `main`/`types` resolve to missing files and imports fail at runtime/type-check time. Add a `"prepare"` (or `"prepublishOnly"`) script that runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json`.

`lint` is an exact duplicate of `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), so the workspace-wide `yarn lint` never runs a real linter; lint/format regressions in this package pass CI silently. Point `lint` at the actual linter configured for the repo (eslint/oxlint) and declare that tool in `devDependencies` (or explicitly document that this package is intentionally unlinted).

`--passWithNoTests` makes `yarn test` succeed even when zero tests are collected (e.g. after an accidental deletion or a broken test glob), so a package with no effective coverage still reports a green suite. Consider dropping the flag for this package, or add a minimum test-count gate, so the absence of tests is surfaced rather than masked.

packages/show-planner/src/color.ts.content: `ensureMinDistance` cannot guarantee its documented "every pair clears minDistance" invariant and fails silently. The hue search probes only 12 fixed +30° steps, and when none is valid the loop exits after the 12th shift wraps the hue back to its starting value — so the function returns the *original, un-repaired* hues with no indication that repair failed. Callers rely on the invariant: `planIdentity` (packages/show-planner/src/identity.ts:55) feeds the result straight into `globalDesign`, and the identity test only passes because it accepts a 0.06 slack below the configured threshold (identity.test.ts:79-81: `paletteMinDistance - 0.06`), which shows the contract is not actually met. A reproducible failure: `ensureMinDistance([{l:0.6,c:0.25,h:0},{l:0.6,c:0.25,h:180}], 0.6)` — the maximum achievable distance for these colours is 2·c = 0.5, so every one of the 12 probes keeps the pair below 0.6 and the violating palette is returned silently. Even for reachable thresholds, a fixed 30° grid can step over a narrow valid window when the colour must clear two neighbours. Signal failure (return a result/flag or throw) and/or use a finer/adversarial scan before abandoning the repair.

`linearRgbToOklab` is exported but has no callers anywhere in the repository (a repo-wide search finds only this declaration), and it is not re-exported from `src/index.ts`. Unlike the other helpers it is not used by `blendRgb`/`blendOklch`. This is dead code that the project's unused-export gate (documented in docs/finish) would flag. Either route it through the renderer/planner path or remove it.

It only hashes two hardcoded JSON strings with node:crypto and asserts the digests differ — it never calls the validation module or any production cache-key/hashing helper, so it passes even if validation returns nothing for the bad input and bad rows would still be cached. Consider asserting the real behavior instead, e.g. that `validateSections([{ startBeat: 5, endBeat: 1 }], beats(32))` is non-empty while the fixed input yields `[]`, and derive the hash from the same helper the production cache actually uses.

Both fixtures are read and JSON.parsed eagerly at module scope. apps/desktop/playwright.config.ts.content: `testDir: "./journeys"` restricts test discovery to the `journeys/` directory, and `testMatch: "**/*.journey.ts"` only accepts `.journey.ts` files. As a result `apps/desktop/e2e/normal-night.spec.ts` (the T-QA-11 17-row acceptance spec for 99-final-acceptance.md section 3) is never collected by `yarn workspace @autolight/desktop test:e2e` — it can never pass or fail. This contradicts docs/finish/evidence/T-QA-11/README.md, which states "the e2e spec is picked up by the same `test:e2e` command", and it matches the documented run ("5 passed": m1-slice + night(2) + soak + live-session = 5 tests over 4 files, i.e. the spec is silently skipped). A silently-unrun acceptance suite means real regressions in those 17 rows go undetected. Either relocate the spec under `journeys/` (e.g. `normal-night.journey.ts`, consistent with e2e/README.md which says the `e2e/` dir stays empty), or widen discovery, e.g. `testDir: "."` with `testMatch: ["**/journeys/**/*.journey.ts", "**/e2e/**/*.spec.ts"]`.

`retries: 0` is set but there is no `forbidOnly` guard. Several journeys (m1-slice, normal-night) are intentionally-red probes whose whole purpose is to fail until dependencies land. If a developer leaves a stray `test.only(...)` on a green test (night/soak/live-session) and pushes, Playwright silently skips all other tests, so CI passes green while the red probes are never evaluated — tests passing despite unverified behavior. Suggest adding the standard CI guard so a committed `.only` fails the run.

apps/desktop/scripts/build-preload.mjs.content: The alias map is built from every raw entry returned by `readdirSync`, with no filtering for directories or for the existence of `src/index.ts`. Stray entries (e.g. `.DS_Store`, stray files, or a non-package directory) produce bogus aliases, and any workspace entry whose directory name differs from the actual package name (or that has no `src/index.ts` barrel) yields an alias that either never matches the import specifier or points at a non-existent file, causing opaque `Could not resolve` build failures that appear only once that package is imported. Filter to real directories whose barrel exists before generating aliases.

`workspaceSrc` hardcodes the relative path `../../packages` with no existence check. If the script is ever run from a different layout (monorepo moved, file relocated, `packages` renamed/removed), `readdirSync` throws a raw `ENOENT` that gives no hint about the expected workspace layout. Consider validating the directory exists and emitting an actionable error.

In `--watch` mode the esbuild context is created and watched but never disposed, and no `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handler is registered, so the rebuild service is left to be torn down implicitly on process exit. More importantly, `ctx.watch()` performs the initial build internally and only logs failures (with `logLevel: "warning"`), so a broken first build still prints `watching ...` and looks successful. Surface the initial build result/errors and dispose the context on termination signals.

  await ctx.watch();

apps/desktop/scripts/build-preload.mjs.content: Both branches `await` esbuild at top level without any `try/catch`, so a build failure bubbles up as an unhandled promise rejection instead of a clean, diagnosable exit; the `bundled ...` log is only reached on success, but there is no `catch` to print a user-facing message or set a non-zero exit code. Wrap the build/watch invocation in a `try/catch` that logs the error and sets `process.exitCode = 1`.

This script is a near-verbatim copy of `build-main.mjs` (imports, `root`/`outElectron`/`workspaceSrc`/`alias` derivation, and the watch/build branch). The duplicated scaffolding must be kept in sync manually — a fix to alias generation or error handling in one file will silently diverge from the other. Consider extracting the shared alias/job/branch logic into a small shared helper module.
